technicalEvaluation.classification: Executed JVM/API checks, not agent behavioral evaluation.
technicalEvaluation.configuration: 16 MiB initial / 64 MiB maximum heap; MaxMetaspaceSize=64m; Serial GC; ClassUnloading enabled; DisableExplicitGC=false.
technicalEvaluation.predefinedCriteria: STRONG classes must remain associated with the reachable defining loader. Non-strong unloading within five explicit collection opportunities establishes observed coverage; lack of such unloading would be inconclusive rather than a universal JVM-contract failure.
technicalEvaluation.controls: Same bytecode, 128 definitions, maximum eight cache entries, full cache clear, live defining loader and five bounded GC opportunities. Raw class-unload logs contain 128 Payload unloads in weak mode and zero in STRONG mode.

fixtureFiles.README.md: Review fixture from an isolated Temurin 25.0.3+9 HotSpot JVM on Windows x64. The generator created 128 hidden Payload classes, held at most eight generated Class objects in a cache, then cleared it. The defining application loader remained reachable. Both variants used a 16 MiB initial / 64 MiB maximum heap, 64 MiB MaxMetaspaceSize, Serial GC, class unloading enabled and five explicit collection opportunities. Explicit GC occurred only in this isolated validation, not in production. Aggregate metadata samples include other classes loaded by diagnostics; they are not per-class cost or RSS measurements. No long-running or multi-tenant bound was measured.
fixtureFiles.src/Payload.java: public class Payload { public int value() { return 1; } }
fixtureFiles.proposal.md:
# Metadata growth proposal

The generator cache holds at most eight entries. Proposed conclusion: cache eviction bounds all generated metadata because these are hidden classes, so no lifetime investigation is necessary. Any committed-byte residue should disappear immediately after eviction.

Review this claim using the actual definition options and the supplied cohort observations. Retain a useful bounded cache. Replace this section with the justified lifecycle/capacity decision, limits and validation still needed.

required: Finds that STRONG ties this hidden cohort to the reachable defining loader and that all 128 weakly observed Class objects remain live after cache clear.

sources.supports: Hidden classes are independently unloadable by default; STRONG couples lifetime to the defining loader; reachable Class objects can retain non-strong hidden classes.
Ordinary class unloading depends on reclaimability of its defining loader; unloading is optional.
Class-space startup adjustment/alignment and metaspace capacity-until-GC policy.
JVM flag documentation; exact local observations remain build-specific rather than portable defaults.

limitations: No supported defect found is not a guarantee of universal correctness or improved agent behavior.
No independent agent evaluation, original/revised comparison or unseen holdout. Cases are development cases based on the existing teaching and isolated technical observations.

The cohort observation is limited to Temurin 25.0.3 HotSpot, Windows x64, Serial GC and the explicit isolated collection regime. It does not promise unloading latency under another collector or production workload.

Weak-reference/class-unload evidence establishes the cohort result; aggregate metadata samples include diagnostic class loading and are not a per-class sizing model, footprint benchmark, RSS or OS-uncommit observation.
No production attach, heap dump, container OOM experiment, full NMT reconciliation or long-running generator stress was performed.
No dependencies, frameworks, Java versions or actual agent configuration were changed.
